newsitem.title: UK: Dlr under pressure at European close, ends mixed.
newsitem.headline: Dlr under pressure at European close, ends mixed.

text.p: The dollar came under selling pressure in late Europe and closed mixed after soft U.S. producer price data dampened U.S. interest rate rise speculation.
"The subdued producer price data erased some of the interest rate rise speculation generated by the retail sales figures," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International.
Dealers also said some longs were liquidated ahead of the weekend after the dollar failed to spurt beyond 1.71 marks and 124 yen.
At 1615 GMT the dollar was at 1.6966/76 marks and 123.18/28 yen, well below session highs at 1.71 and 124.11. At Thursday's European close, the dollar was at 1.7022/32 and 122.98/123.05.

Initial dollar/mark strength was capped by a rise in the mark/yen cross, which helped boost dollar/yen. The dollar's decline against the mark gathered momentum on the break below 1.70 marks and stops were triggered at 1.6980, dealers said.
"The late sell-off here now brings the overnight low at 1.69 back into focus," said a senior trader at a German bank.
The 0.4-percent drop in the producer price index in February was the largest since October 1994.
The market had expected a 0.1-percent decline. Ex-food and energy, the index fell 0.1 percent against an expected 0.1-percent rise.

February industrial production and capacity use data showed the U.S. economy remained strong. Industrial production rose 0.5 percent, as expected, and capacity use stood at 83.3, slightly lower than forecasts for 83.5.

"The dollar will now keep an eye on next week's consumer price data," said Stamenkovic. "In terms of rate rise hopes, we have retail sales growing above trend, but if inflation remains on the soft side, support for the dollar might be waning."
